Maintenance Report — MNT-0118-015

Asset: WELL-0118 (NE-07 Well 118, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 17 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 04 Jun 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 425 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0118-0134 on 2025-05-15 Report written: 04 Jun 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0118-0134 showed the wellhead at 27.8 °C with the air at 24.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 249 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 199 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0118-015 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0118-019

Asset: WELL-0118 (NE-07 Well 118, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 02 Nov 2025 08:00 · Finished: 18 Nov 2025 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 385 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0118-0157 on 2025-10-30 Report written: 20 Nov 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0118-0157 showed the wellhead at 24.6 °C with the air at 20.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.
